name: Carmen Whitehead
blurb: Carmen Whitehead (Democratic, Green River). Reached the 2024 general-election ballot after a Democratic primary write-in campaign. Lost the Nov. 5, 2024 general election for State House HD60 with 951 votes (27.7%).
occupation: Has worked in the Third Judicial District Court and later for the Sweetwater County Engineering, Planning and Zoning department (Rocket Miner, Nov. 2, 2024)
background: Carmen Whitehead is a Democrat from Green River who ran for House District 60 in 2024. The Rocket Miner reported on Nov. 2, 2024, that she reached the general-election ballot through a write-in campaign. Ballotpedia’s election results also list her as a write-in winner of the Aug. 20, 2024 Democratic primary. She lost the Nov. 5, 2024 general election.

The same Rocket Miner profile, drawing on a press release from Whitehead, said she is the daughter of an iron-ore miner and a stay-at-home mother, and that her father helped organize a union at the CF&I mine in Sunrise, Wyoming. Locally, the article said, she has worked in the Third Judicial District Court and later transferred to the Sweetwater County Engineering, Planning and Zoning department. It also reported that she was a delegate twice at State Democratic conventions and chaired the Supervisory Committee for the Green River Basin Federal Credit Union for numerous years.

name: Martha J. Wright
blurb: Martha J. Wright (Democratic, Sheridan). Lost the Nov. 5, 2024 general election for State House HD29 with 1,325 votes (30.6%), after also running for the same seat in 2022.
occupation: Experience in the medical field, criminal justice, church work, and, as of a June 2022 Sheridan Press announcement, the YMCA
background: Martha J. Wright of Sheridan ran as a Democrat for House District 29 in 2022 and 2024, losing both general elections. In 2024 she reached the general-election ballot as a Democratic primary write-in (Ballotpedia); the official general result on the WyoVote Profile is 1,325 votes (30.6%).

The Sheridan Press reported on June 3, 2022, when she declared her first candidacy, that she was born in Casper, raised in Cheyenne, and graduated from Cheyenne East High School, and that her life and work had taken her out of state and back to Wyoming. The article said her experience had included work in the medical field, criminal justice, her church, and, at the time of that announcement, the YMCA, and that she described her life as one of service.
education: Cheyenne East High School (The Sheridan Press, June 3, 2022)

name: Richard Brubaker
blurb: Richard Brubaker (Libertarian, Riverton): Truck driver. Lost the Nov. 5, 2024 general election for U.S. House with 9,223 votes (3.5%).
residence: Riverton, Fremont County (2024 SOS general candidate list)
occupation: Truck driver; formerly a dairy farmer (Wyoming Tribune-Eagle, 2012; Thermopolis Independent Record, 2024)
background: Richard Brubaker of Riverton was the Libertarian nominee for Wyoming’s at-large U.S. House seat in 2024 and lost the Nov. 5 general election with 9,223 votes (3.5%). The official 2024 general candidate list gives a Riverton mailing address.

The Thermopolis Independent Record, in an Oct. 31, 2024 federal-candidate summary, said he lives in Riverton, attended Central Wyoming College and the University of Wyoming, is a truck driver, and had also been a U.S. House candidate in 2014, 2018, 2020, and 2022. Ballotpedia likewise describes him as a truck driver and records earlier Libertarian U.S. House runs, including 2012.

A Sept. 21, 2012 Wyoming Tribune-Eagle profile said the then-59-year-old Riverton resident had been a dairy farmer before becoming a truck driver in 1998, had graduated from Wind River High School and had some college at Central Wyoming College, and had previously run unsuccessfully for House District 34 three times.
education: Wind River High School; attended Central Wyoming College and the University of Wyoming (Wyoming Tribune-Eagle, 2012; Thermopolis Independent Record, 2024)

name: Timothy (Tim) Forbis
blurb: Timothy (Tim) Forbis (Independent, Cheyenne): Real estate broker. Lost the Nov. 5, 2024 general election for State House HD10 with 865 votes (17.9%).
occupation: Real estate broker; CEO and president of real estate corporations operating in Wyoming, Colorado, and Nebraska (campaign site; Shriners International biography)
background: Timothy (Tim) Forbis of Cheyenne ran as an Independent for House District 10 in 2024 and lost the Nov. 5 general election with 865 votes (17.9%). The Wyoming Tribune-Eagle reported on Oct. 25, 2024, that the Cheyenne resident successfully petitioned to run as an independent after the primary. The official general candidate list records a Cheyenne address and an Aug. 26, 2024 filing date.

His campaign site, forbis4hd10.com, describes him as a real-estate broker born and raised in Laramie County, and says he serves on the Board of Directors for Shriners Children’s Hospitals and is involved in helping small towns develop. The same site said he was approached late in the cycle to run as an Independent.

A Shriners International leadership biography says he worked in the hospitality and entertainment industry until 1997, when he went into real estate; that he is CEO and president of two real-estate corporations operating in Colorado, Wyoming, and Nebraska; that he has taught property management and investment real estate; and that he graduated from Natrona County High School in 1979 and from trade schools for management, business, and broadcasting. In 2026 he was elected Imperial Oriental Guide of Shriners International (Shriners International biography).
education: Natrona County High School, 1979; trade-school study in management, business, and broadcasting (Shriners International biography)
